tools.name: workflow
tools.description:
Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. A stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) end the whole script instead of producing `null`. The script has no filesystem, network, timer, or Node.js APIs; the agents do the work.

script.description: The plain JavaScript body, not TypeScript and without an `export const meta` statement; top-level await is allowed. End with `return <value>`; the JSON-serializable value is this tool's result.

description.description: One-line description of what the workflow does.

whenToUse.description: Optional guidance on when this workflow applies.

provider.description: Optional provider override this phase is expected to use.

args.description: Optional JSON input exposed to the script as the `args` global (wrap a bare list as a field, e.g. {"files": [...]}).

run_in_background.description: Run as a background job: return a job id immediately instead of waiting; the return value arrives with the completion notice.

Implement parse_duration: parse string with optional spaces, case-insensitive units, order decreasing, each unit at most once; also if only integer with no unit => seconds. Accept "0s" and "0". Otherwise raise ValueError.

Implementation approach:

- Strip whitespace
- If text after strip is empty: raise ValueError
- If matches only digits: return int(digits) (ensure non-negative)
- Else parse tokens: use regex to find (integer)(unit) optionally separated by spaces.
- Must ensure the entire string is consumed (except spaces).
- Use pattern: r'(?i)\s*(\d+)([dhms])\s*' repeated.
Simpler: iterate through characters, building tokens.

Also enforce order: define order mapping {'d':0,'h':1,'m':2,'s':3}. Ensure tokens appear with non-decreasing order index (i.e., decreasing time => order indexes must be non-decreasing as we go: d (0) then h (1) etc). Actually order decreasing means d before h before m before s. So indexes must be non-decreasing, not decreasing.

Also ensure each unit appears at most once: track seen set.

def parse_duration(text):
    if not isinstance(text,str): raise ValueError
    s=text.strip()
    if s=='':
        raise ValueError
    # all digits?
    if s.isdigit():
        return int(s)
    # else parse components
    import re
    pattern=re.compile(r'(?i)\s*(\d+)([dhms])')
    pos=0
    total=0
    last_index= -1
    seen=set()
    while pos < len(s):
        m=pattern.match(s,pos)
        if not m:
            raise ValueError
        number=int(m.group(1))
        unit=m.group(2).lower()
        if unit in seen:
            raise ValueError
        seen.add(unit)
        cur_index = dict(d=0,h=1,m=2,s=3)[unit]
        if cur_index < last_index:
            raise ValueError
        last_index = cur_index
        # find size
        size = dict(d=86400,h=3600,m=60,s=1)[unit]
        total += number*size
        pos = m.end()
        # After a component may be spaces. Continue loop.
    # After loop ensure only spaces remain
    if s[pos:].strip():
        raise ValueError
    return total

Edge cases: negative numbers not allowed because pattern only digits (no "-"). Decimal not allowed.

    # Implementation based on the specification above.
    if not isinstance(text, str):
        raise ValueError("duration must be a string")
    s = text.strip()
    if s == "":
        raise ValueError("empty duration string")
    # If the string is just digits, interpret as seconds.
    if s.isdigit():
        return int(s)
    # Mapping of unit to its size in seconds and order index.
    unit_to_seconds = {"d": 86400, "h": 3600, "m": 60, "s": 1}
    unit_order = {"d": 0, "h": 1, "m": 2, "s": 3}
    import re
    pattern = re.compile(r"(?i)\s*(\d+)([dhms])")
    pos = 0
    total = 0
    seen = set()
    last_index = -1
    while pos < len(s):
        m = pattern.match(s, pos)
        if not m:
            raise ValueError(f"invalid duration component at: '{s[pos:]}'")
        number = int(m.group(1))
        unit = m.group(2).lower()
        # Check duplicate units.
        if unit in seen:
            raise ValueError(f"duplicate unit '{unit}' in duration")
        seen.add(unit)
        # Enforce decreasing order (d > h > m > s).
        cur_index = unit_order[unit]
        if cur_index < last_index:
            raise ValueError("units out of order in duration")
        last_index = cur_index
        total += number * unit_to_seconds[unit]
        pos = m.end()
    # Ensure any trailing characters are only whitespace.
    if s[pos:].strip():

    return total
